thread:
maria (runtime): seeing a sharp p99 tail after last midnight deploy, first noticed ~02:15 UTC. p50/p95 fine but p99 jumped to ~820ms on generation-only routes.
aj (infra): confirmed in metrics — spike aligns with canary rollover at 02:12. traces show a subset of requests with huge KV lookup time.
maria (runtime): digging into traces: pattern -> very long context prompts (~8k-12k tokens) + tool-call loop (client triggers multiple tool calls), kernel picker switched to fp16-gemm-async variant mid-request. logs: `kernel_pick=fp16_gemm_async, seq_len=8192, microbatch=8`
cheng (serving): that combo is rough: fp16_gemm_async has better throughput for short sequences but its kernel launch latency and async sync points penalize very long KV walks. microbatch=8 exacerbates latency when one request hogs KV due to prefix cache misses.
maria (runtime): pulled a flamegraph from the agent:
```
GPU kernels: 45% attention, 25% matmul, 20% kernel-sync stalls
KV lookup: 380ms (blocking)
Host GPU sync: 120ms
Total host-to-host stalls: 530ms
```
aj (infra): ran quick A/B: microbatch_floor=2 vs 8 for the affected model. results: p99 820ms -> 310ms, p95 ~ stable, overall throughput -11% at peak. tradeoff seems reasonable for latency SLO routes.
maria (runtime): also saw repeated cache evictions; requests with tool calls cause many short live KV segments, eviction churn. kv_hit_ratio drops to 0.32 for those sessions.
cheng (serving): two-pronged mitigation: 1) route long-context/tool-call-heavy requests to a "longseq" pool with microbatch_floor=1 and a kernel variant tuned for long attention (sync-friendly), 2) prefix-aware KV pinning for active sessions so we avoid evicting between tool calls.
aj (infra): implemented a canary for route-level policy (policy: if seq_len_estimate>4096 or tool_call_count>1 -> longseq_pool). infra-bot: canary deploy started 1965432140, hosts=6 -> 6, rolling 2/6.
maria (runtime): quick perf run on canary: p99 trimmed to 340ms for routed traffic, overall infra throughput drop on those hosts ~9% but end-to-end SLO satisfied. need to validate at higher qps.
cheng (serving): kernel chooser patch: prefer sync-optimized kernels when seq_len>4096 OR kv_miss_rate>0.25. small change but test shows 8-12% tail improvement on synthetic long prompts.
sre-oncall: opening incident/perf ticket with these notes and marking as action items: 1) route policy rollout plan, 2) prefix pinning feature spec, 3) kernel-chooser flag and perf regression dashboard.
aj (infra): +1. also flagging that microbatch_floor is a global param on some pools — we'll need route-scoped override capability.
maria (runtime): follow-ups: run load test with mixed long prompt+tool loops at 2x production qps, confirm KV pinning doesn't cause memory leaks, add a regression check in perf-tests for p99 on longseq routes.
cheng (serving): I'll sketch the prefix pinning design (LRU-with-reservation) and a fallback eviction threshold. prototype by EOD tomorrow.
infra-bot: canary deploy completed 1965432270, health=ok, metrics: p99 improved for canary route.
maria (runtime): thanks — we should avoid flipping global microbatch_floor until route overrides exist. putting a hold on global changes. :thumbsup:
aj (infra): noted. will document the canary results and open PR for route overrides.
sre-oncall: thanks team — adding postmortem label and tracking in incidents. if anyone sees a regression after full rollout ping here
